published_or_source_claim.mechanism: Given exact sampled values from a monotone cooperative game, maximize each target player's Shapley linear functional over all monotone completions consistent with those observations. The resulting maximum is a deterministic upper bound; because the Boolean-lattice order polytope is integral, the LP can be solved exactly as a maximum-weight closure / s-t min-cut problem.
published_or_source_claim.reported_holdout: For the fixed 10-player synthetic game and unseen seeds 1000..1999, the source reports phi<=0.005 certification for rare players 8/9 at 62.2%/61.9% by 896 unique coalition calls, with exact completion at 1024 calls and zero false certifications.
published_or_source_claim.scope_stated_by_source: Confirmatory unseen-seed holdout on the same fixed game only; exact binary oracle and global monotonicity required; no independent-game generalization claim.

external_theory_support.reference: Richard P. Stanley, Two Poset Polytopes, Discrete & Computational Geometry 1 (1986), DOI 10.1007/BF02187680
external_theory_support.relevance: Order-polytope vertices are 0/1 characteristic functions of order filters/upper sets. Fixing observed coordinates to 0 or 1 restricts to a face, so an optimum of the Shapley linear functional is attained at a monotone binary completion.

external_theory_support.reference: Jean-Claude Picard, Maximal Closure of a Graph and Applications to Combinatorial Problems, Management Science 22(11) (1976), DOI 10.1287/mnsc.22.11.1268
external_theory_support.relevance: Maximum-weight closure on a directed graph is the exact combinatorial optimization problem induced by upper-set constraints and is reducible to min-cut/max-flow.

rare_player_truth.player_8: The only positive predecessor coalition is {0,2,4,6,9}; all paired supports must remain incomplete and adding 8 then completes {0,2,4,6,8,9}. Its Shapley weight is 5!*4!/10! = 1/1260.
rare_player_truth.player_9: Symmetrically the only positive predecessor coalition is {0,2,4,6,8}; the same weight gives 1/1260.

closure_network_capacity_check.finite_positive_weight_sum: For any player, sum_k C(9,k) k!(9-k)! = 10*9! = 10!.
closure_network_capacity_check.assessment: One cut through an INF precedence/fixed-value arc costs ten times the total positive objective weight, so no optimum can profit by violating a monotonicity or fixed-observation constraint. The finite-capacity construction is therefore sufficient for this n=10 objective.

solver_equivalence.assessment: The preregistered target is the LP optimum over a face of the order polytope. Replacing a generic LP solver with the mathematically equivalent maximum-weight closure/max-flow implementation does not change the optimization target. The source's eight linprog spot checks are supportive but are not needed for the structural equivalence claim once the closure reduction is established.

independent_analytic_reproduction.full_observation_check: At 1024 observed coalition values the feasible completion is unique, so the upper bound must equal the exact Shapley value 1/1260 for both rare players. The reported 1024-call result matches this invariant.

reproducibility_limits.full_1000_seed_matched_rerun: Not independently reproduced in this audit. The 62.2%/61.9% and intermediate-budget certification rates remain source-run numerical evidence, although the safety property of every returned bound is analytically supported under the stated assumptions.
reproducibility_limits.environment_pinning: The three v1 artifacts bind the game, seed transform, budgets, thresholds and code, but they do not themselves record an exact Python/SciPy environment or container digest. Therefore seed-to-order and solver replay are not fully environment-immutable from these artifacts alone.
reproducibility_limits.external_independent_replication: No protocol-matched independent third-party rerun of this synthetic v1 experiment was established in this audit.
reproducibility_limits.generalization: No evidence here establishes useful certification rates on independent game families, nonmonotone games, noisy oracles or large lemma pools. The explicit Boolean lattice is exponential in n.

scope_correction: Treat zero false certifications as a deterministic consequence of exact-oracle monotonicity plus exact optimization, not as empirical evidence of calibration quality. The decision-relevant empirical quantity is how early the deterministic bound becomes useful. The reported 896-call ~62% rate is promising for this one fixed game, but it is not independently reproduced here and cannot be generalized beyond the preregistered fixed-game holdout.
downstream_implication: C552 can be used as strong evidence that trusted monotonicity can turn partial exact observations into a valid deterministic Shapley upper bound and that max-closure is an exact implementation route. Do not use the reported certification-rate curve as independent-game evidence, and do not transfer the certificate to noisy/nonmonotone utility without a new proof.
reopen_or_upgrade_conditions: a protocol-matched independent rerun of all 1000 frozen seeds
an immutable Python/SciPy/container environment binding for exact replay
the preregistered independent-game generator and holdout results requested by the source frontier
a compressed/symbolic certifier with a proof preserving the same monotone-completion upper bound at larger n
a noisy-oracle or approximate-monotonicity extension with a separate valid uncertainty proof
exact_next_action: Move to a different source-qualified C24 candidate unless one of the upgrade conditions appears. Prefer an under-audited member with runnable official artifacts or a claim whose exact numerical result can be independently reconstructed without repeating C552.
